key_insight: Execution-state capsules checkpoint and restore the full graph-bound runtime state—not just KV cache—enabling fast, exact reuse for low-latency on-device AI serving.
engineering_relevance: This lets interactive agents, speech stacks, and robot policies recover, branch, and re-enter execution with much lower time-to-first-token than cold prefill on GPU and edge hardware.
method: FlashRT captures execution plans over contiguous static buffers with no block-table indirection.
A capsule snapshots/restores the complete committed boundary, including KV, recurrent, convolution, MTP state, and metadata.
Supports fork/rollback of execution state for graph-bound reuse rather than token-bound KV reuse.
evidence_signal: On an RTX 5090, restore was byte-exact and greedy decoding was token-identical; TTFT speedup over cold prefill rose from 3.9x at 2k tokens to 27x at 16k tokens, with sub-millisecond GPU-resident snapshot/restore.
watch_item: This approach depends on a white-box, backend-facing runtime with closed-set named buffers, so integrating arbitrary or dynamic model runtimes may be non-trivial.
paper_title: Execution-State Capsules: Graph-Bound Execution-State Checkpoint and Restore for Low-Latency, Small-Batch, On-Device Physical-AI Serving
